LESSON: WRITING 2.3.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing, part of Strand 2 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is punctuation important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify imperatives from a written text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use punctuation marks (the hyphen, apostrophe, bracket

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

S. in a written text for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the place of punctuation in writing for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify imperatives from a written text for comprehension,

   Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use punctuation marks (the hyphen, apostrophe, bracket

   Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. in a written text for effective communication,

   Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the place of punctuation in writing for effective communication.

   Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a text discussing environmental conservation with peers,

2. pick out imperatives from a text on environmental conservation,

3. collaborate with peers to punctuate a text using the target punctuation marks (the hyphen, apostrophe, bracket or any other language specific punctuation mark),

4. take turns to assess each other’s work,

5. work jointly to draw the various punctuation marks on flashcards and display in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a text discussing environmental conservation with peers,
2. pick out imperatives from a text on environmental conservation,
3. collaborate with peers to punctuate a text using the target punctuation marks (the hyphen, apostrophe, bracket or any other language specific punctuation mark),
4. take turns to assess each other’s work,
5. work jointly to draw the various punctuation marks on flashcards and display in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.3.1 Mechanics of writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner works harmoniously with peers to punctuate a text using the target

punctuation marks.

• Learning to Learn: This is nurtured as the learner contributes to collective learning by assessing their peers' work

and making necessary corrections for improvement.

12

Values:
● Unity: This is cultivated as the learner cooperates with peers to discuss topics on environment conservation.

● Respect: This is developed as the learner appreciates the ideas from peers as they assess each other’s work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: This is promoted as the learner interacts with information on environmental conversation.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concepts on environmental conservation to their learning of similar content in Agriculture.

Main points to remember:

1. identify imperatives from a written text for comprehension,
